column1: # MosoFin skill explainers — tracker. One row per skill; this file is the source of truth for the site.
# Explainer kinds: plain (business owners) · learn (worked levels, cited) · anatomy (how it is built).

column10: summary
Checks that what Stripe, Square or PayPal says you were paid matches your books, and catches revenue recorded net of processor fees.
column11: Plain page cites Stripe, Square, PayPal and the IRS; learn page adds IFRS 10.

column10: Finds the costs and income that belong to this period but are not in the books yet, and proposes the entries and their reversals.
Finds goods and services you received before period end but have not been billed for, and proposes the accrual so costs land in the right month.
Ages what you owe suppliers, flags what is overdue or disputed, and proposes a payment run in priority order for a person to approve.
Ages what customers owe you as of a date you choose, ties it to the books, and ranks who to chase first, with drafts for review.
Ties each balance sheet account to its support, names every difference, and says which balances are proved and which still need evidence.
Proves your bank statement and your books differ only for reasons you can name (timing, fees, bounced items) and finds what is left over.
column11: Plain page cites the FDIC, IRS, CFPB, NAUPA, GAO, Intuit and Stripe; learn page adds IFRS 10. Anatomy page: all 4 audit findings fixed on main (79f7a93, 2197ec8); skill now in card format.

column10: Compares the month's results to budget, explains the variances that matter, and checks the month is closed before explaining anything.
Matches customer payments to open invoices, handles short pays, overpayments and fees, and sends what it cannot explain to a person.
Builds a week-by-week cash forecast for the next quarter, starting from cash agreed to the bank, without counting the same bill twice.
Prepares the year-end closing entries, including owner draws and member allocations, and proves the post-closing trial balance.
Ties the company card statement to your books, matches receipts to charges, and lists what is missing, personal, duplicated or in the wrong account.
column11: Plain and learn pages cite the IRS, HMRC, the CFPB, Intuit, ACFE and IFRS 10. Both audit findings fixed in the card-format split of 25 Oct; see the anatomy page.

column10: Builds credit memos and refunds with the right offsetting entry, so revenue and tax are reversed once and only once.
Drafts customer invoices and checks their fields, numbering and totals, with the receivable, revenue and tax entry that balances.
Scans payables for invoices that may be entered or paid twice, scores how likely each pair is, and shows the money at risk.
Reviews employee expense claims against your policy, catches duplicates and card charges claimed twice, and works out what each person is owed.
Builds the statement set from your books with the tie-outs that prove it, and says plainly which statements it could not produce.
Keeps the fixed asset register, works out depreciation under your policy, and catches assets booked as expenses or disposals booked wrong.
Suggests the account for each transaction from your own posting history, and flags money coming in that may already be counted as a sale.
Ties inventory counts and item values to the balance in your books at the count date, and names what explains the difference.
Reads supplier invoices into structured data, checks the arithmetic and tax, and warns before a bill that may already be paid is entered.
Builds a journal entry against your real chart of accounts and checks it before anyone posts it, so a balanced entry is also a correct one.
Screens every journal entry in a period for risk, after first proving the list is complete, and explains why each flagged entry was flagged.
Runs the month-end close as a checklist built from your own books, with an owner for every step and proof the prior month did not change.
Itemises what is left in the payroll clearing and liability accounts, ages it, and says who is owed what before anything is written off.
Builds the entries that record a payroll run, with gross-to-net, employer costs and accruals, at account level and never person by person.
Ties the payroll register to the books, the bank and what was paid to the tax authorities, and says plainly which checks could not be run.
Builds and checks the prepaid expense schedule, so insurance, software and other costs paid ahead are spread over the months they cover.
Designs a recurring entry, bill or invoice schedule, checks it does not already exist, and later audits whether every occurrence ran.
Checks that what you ordered, what arrived and what the supplier billed agree, line by line, before anything is paid, and says which of the three it had.
column11: Plain and learn pages cite the FAR, ACFE, GAO, IFRS, Intuit and NY Tax. Anatomy page: all three audit findings fixed on main (4d5637c, 9882a07, 526d8bf); skill now in card format.

column10: Ties a supplier's statement to what your books say you owe, item by item, and lists missing invoices, credits and payments in transit.

Build an interactive, single-file cash forecast dashboard for a multi-entity business (several QuickBooks company files) in a fixed "quiet analytics" visual style, with per-entity and consolidated views, P10/P90 forecast band, accounts/rece
